name: Northern Mexico (Chihuahua · Sonora · Nuevo León · Coahuila)

language.script_notes: ALTO stop signs, 'topes', -MEX company names. English is more visible here than elsewhere in Mexico because of the border and maquiladora industry.

road_furniture.guardrail_type: Steel W-beam; concrete barrier on the wide toll roads that carry freight to the US.
road_furniture.line_paint: White edge and yellow centre lines; long straight well-marked desert highways.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Octagonal or crucifix concrete poles. OXXO everywhere; more US chains (fast food, big-box stores) near the border than in the rest of Mexico.

architecture.roof_style: Low, flat concrete roofs with tinacos; wider spacing between buildings.
architecture.roof_material: Concrete slab; some sheet metal on ranch buildings.
architecture.wall_construction: Brick and concrete block, more of it rendered and finished than in the south; adobe on older rural houses; big modern industrial and residential development around Monterrey.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Beige, tan and pale earth tones; less of the vivid painting seen further south.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Spread-out, car-oriented border towns; ranch (rancho) compounds; modern glass towers and industrial parks in Monterrey; US-style strip malls near the frontier.

nature.vegetation: Chihuahuan and Sonoran desert — creosote scrub, ocotillo, yucca, and tall saguaro cactus in Sonora — with dry grassland on the plateaus and pine forest only high in the Sierra Madre Occidental.
nature.terrain: Basin and range: wide flat desert valleys between bare rocky ranges, the deep Copper Canyon in the Sierra Madre, and flat coastal desert in Sonora.
nature.climate_signature: Hot desert days, cold desert nights, very little rain (a summer monsoon bump in Sonora). Dusty air, hard shadows, sparse tan vegetation.

vehicles.plate_color: State plates — Chihuahua, Sonora, Nuevo León and Coahuila each with their own design and name banner.
vehicles.plate_format: State-dependent, commonly three letters and three–four digits.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: A higher share of American pickups (Ford, RAM, Chevrolet Silverado) and older US imports; lots of freight trucks; often dusty.

google_coverage.coverage_notes: Long empty desert-highway stretches between towns.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Sonoran/Chihuahuan desert, saguaro, wide roads and ranch land continue straight across the border into Arizona, New Mexico and Texas
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Spanish signage, Mexican state plates, OXXO, 'topes' and rooftop tinacos; the US side has English signs, US plates and no speed bumps on highways.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country — ALTO, OXXO, tinacos, state plates
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The north is flat hot desert with cactus, spread-out towns and more US influence; the centre is a cooler pine-oak highland plateau with volcanoes, agave and dense colonial cities.
